chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Ibrahim ibn Ahmad ibn Hisham al-Mu'addab (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Abu'l Husayn Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Asadi narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Bazi' narrated to me. He said: Abu'l Hasan Ali ibn Musa al-Rida (peace be upon him) said,

regarding the saying of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: "Sight comprehends Him not, yet He comprehends all sight" [6:103]. He said: The imaginations of the hearts cannot comprehend Him, so how could the sight of eyes comprehend Him?!

key_terms.أوهام القلوب: Imaginations of the hearts — the inner faculty of perception and imagination, considered more subtle than physical sight
key_terms.لا تدركه الأبصار: Sight comprehends Him not — a Quranic statement (6:103) used as proof-text against the possibility of physically seeing God

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Rida say about seeing God and the meaning of Quran 6:103?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (as) provides a commentary on Quran 6:103, which states that sight cannot perceive God. He deepens the meaning by explaining that if even the imaginations of the hearts — which are more subtle and far-reaching than physical sight — cannot comprehend God, then physical eyesight is even more incapable of doing so. This is part of a broader theological tradition in Shi'a Islam that firmly rejects the possibility of seeing God with physical eyes, a position debated among different Muslim schools of thought.
